subject: POC trial blueprint & acceptance checklist — LumenScale
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Brooks <aisha.b@lumenscale.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@lumenscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial blueprint & acceptance checklist — LumenScale

Thanks for a good kickoff earlier — appreciate the clarity on your evaluation goals. Per our conversation, I pulled together a short blueprint for the 4-week POC so we can align on success criteria, who owns what, and what you’ll need to validate in each week.

Summary (ask: confirm or update by Thu EOD):
- Goal: Validate LumenScale search/QA feature powered by Redwood inference for production-like queries at ~99% intent match and average latency < 280ms p50 on the 2k test queries.
- Duration: 4 weeks (sandbox + smoke -> load -> ops handoff).
- Primary metrics: quality (precision@1 / intent match), latency (p50/p95), throughput (requests/s sustained), and cost (approx. cost/token estimate).

High-level plan
1) Week 0 (this week): Data ingest + baseline
  - You provide anonymized sample (we received LS_POC_Data_Sample.csv).
  - Redwood runs initial smoke and returns baseline metrics and tokenized cost estimate.
2) Week 1: Model tuning and latency baseline
  - Measure p50/p95 across batch and single-request modes. Goal p50 < 280ms, p95 < 600ms.
3) Week 2: Throughput and cost profiling
  - Ramp to target QPS (TBD). Capture tokens per request, CPU/GPU utilization, and cost/token projections.
4) Week 3: Quality validation & ops handoff
  - Run your 2k evaluation queries, produce precision@1 and human review sample.
  - Produce acceptance report and recommended guardrails for production.

Ownership
- LumenScale: provide sanitized dataset, evaluation queries, and sign-off on quality targets.
- Redwood (Markus/Marissa): infra, experiment configs, latency/throughput measurements, weekly report.
- Ops contact (Ben): onboarding checklist for Dedicated/Demo environment and any procurement items.

Acceptance criteria (proposed, please counter if needed):
- Quality: precision@1 >= 0.88 on the 2k query set (human-evaluated sample must not show systemic hallucination).
- Latency: p50 < 280ms, p95 < 600ms at baseline traffic (1–5 RPS per shard).
- Throughput: sustain 100 RPS across a 3-min ramp with less than 10% p95 degradation.
- Cost: projected average cost/token reduction <= 30% relative to your current provider baseline (we'll model once we ingest tokens).

Attachments: shared LS_POC_Data_Sample.csv and a blank POC-Acceptance-Template-v1.xlsx for you to confirm the acceptance cells.

Next steps
- Aisha/Tom: confirm the proposed acceptance criteria and the target QPS you want us to model (reply by Thu).
- LumenScale procurement: if you want us to provision a reserved sandbox or sign an NDA, loop procurement and I’ll send an SOW stub.

Thanks — I’ll start the baseline run once you confirm.

—
Markus Klein
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

From: Aisha Brooks <aisha.b@lumenscale.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@lumenscale.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial blueprint & acceptance checklist — LumenScale

Thanks Markus — this is helpful and maps to what we discussed. Quick confirmations and a couple of edits: 

- We can commit to the 4-week cadence.
- Target QPS: model for both 50 RPS steady-state and a 200 RPS burst scenario (our read replicas will see spikes).
- Quality: we’re comfortable with precision@1 >= 0.88 as a starting point, but we want a secondary guard of <5% non-actionable/unsafe responses on a 500-sample human review.
- Latency: p50 < 300ms is fine if you can get p95 <= 650ms for the burst profile. If not, propose alternatives.

I loaded the data sample and removed the PII columns. Sharing procurement separately.

A couple of asks: please add an explicit rollback/fallback plan if quality regressions appear during the trial, and include the model variant you’ll start with. Also can you add a row in the acceptance template for "human review pass rate"?

Will loop procurement this afternoon.

Best,
Aisha
Head of Product | LumenScale
aisha.b@lumenscale.com | +1 212-555-0117

Thanks Aisha — good notes. I made the edits you requested and attached an updated POC-Acceptance-Template-v1.xlsx with the extra "Human review pass rate" row and a small rollback checklist. Key updates below: 

- Model variant: we'll start on rdx-compat-v2 (8-bit quantized) for lower token cost and iterate to rdx-compat-v3 if quality needs improvement.
- Rollback/fallback: default fallback -> rdx-compat-v1 (unquantized) + capacity throttling; automated alerting to both teams if human review fails 3 checks in a row.
- Burst profile target: p95<=700ms during 200 RPS burst with graceful degradation (we'll surface tradeoffs in the week-2 cost/throughput report).

I kicked off the baseline ingest this morning — attaching the initial smoke run log (summary included in the attached template tab "Week0-Baseline").

Action items: 
- LumenScale: confirm procurement contact for an SOW (procurement@lumenscale.com) and confirm the 200 RPS burst requirement.
- Redwood: Marissa and I will run the Week 1 latency matrix and tag results in the shared drive link; Ben will scope Dedicated sandbox cost if you prefer reserved capacity.

Markus

Attachments referenced: POC-Acceptance-Template-v1.xlsx (updated), LS_POC_Data_Sample.csv (received)

Looping in on the ops/procurement side. A few quick notes on Dedicated sandbox and cost expectations so procurement has context: 

- Dedicated sandbox (recommended for realistic throughput tests): estimated monthly baseline = $6,200 (includes reserved GPU capacity for the 4-week trial window and extra I/O for dataset ingest). Final number depends on region and whether you want burst credits.
- If you prefer hosted ephemeral: we can run the same experiments but will throttle burst testing to stay within trial credits; that will affect p95 under the 200 RPS scenario.
- Procurement: I'll prepare a short SOW + pricing addendum and a DocuSign link once you confirm sandbox vs hosted.

Next steps from ops side:
- LumenScale confirms sandbox request (yes/no).
- Procurement confirms billing contact and PO window.
